requirements.title: BLT arguments are integer or BOZ bit sequences
requirements.definition: The I and J arguments to BLT shall each be of type integer or be a BOZ literal constant.

pending.blt-i-integer-or-boz: Use a guarded generated most-significant-bit BOZ literal matched to z=BIT_SIZE(0): for z==32 emit MSB_BOZ=Z'80000000' and ONE_BOZ=Z'00000001', and for z==64 emit MSB_BOZ=Z'8000000000000000' and ONE_BOZ=Z'0000000000000001'; extend the generator table only with literals of exactly z bits and emit only the matching supported-z case, so the source never relies on a BOZ length the processor need not support. This uses no INT(boz) value semantics: 16.9.49 p6 says a boz-literal-constant argument is interpreted as the bit sequence described in 7.7; 7.7 p1 says such a constant has no type; 7.7 p2 says each hexadecimal digit represents four bits and the literal is the concatenation of those bit sequences; and 16.3.2 compares the resulting bit sequences from the left, padding shorter sequences with zero bits if necessary. There is no largest-kind or other-integer-kind conversion rule for these bit-comparison intrinsics; a both-BOZ control compares the two 7.7 bit sequences directly. With result initialized to .true., assert BLT(MSB_BOZ,1) is .false. because the BOZ sequence starts with 1 and the nonnegative integer 1 sequence has leading zero bits; also assert BLT(ONE_BOZ,MSB_BOZ) is .true. for both BOZ actuals. Mutate MSB_BOZ to an all-zero z-bit BOZ literal so the mixed-actual assertion fails. Wrong-type source controls are unnumbered and expect no local diagnostic.
pending.blt-j-integer-or-boz: Use a guarded generated most-significant-bit BOZ literal matched to z=BIT_SIZE(0): for z==32 emit MSB_BOZ=Z'80000000' and ONE_BOZ=Z'00000001', and for z==64 emit MSB_BOZ=Z'8000000000000000' and ONE_BOZ=Z'0000000000000001'; extend the generator table only with literals of exactly z bits and emit only the matching supported-z case, so the source never relies on a BOZ length the processor need not support. This uses no INT(boz) value semantics: 16.9.49 p6 says a boz-literal-constant argument is interpreted as the bit sequence described in 7.7; 7.7 p1 says such a constant has no type; 7.7 p2 says each hexadecimal digit represents four bits and the literal is the concatenation of those bit sequences; and 16.3.2 compares the resulting bit sequences from the left, padding shorter sequences with zero bits if necessary. There is no largest-kind or other-integer-kind conversion rule for these bit-comparison intrinsics; a both-BOZ control compares the two 7.7 bit sequences directly. With result initialized to .false., assert BLT(1,MSB_BOZ) is .true. because the nonnegative integer 1 sequence has leading zero bits and the BOZ sequence starts with 1; also assert BLT(ONE_BOZ,MSB_BOZ) is .true. for both BOZ actuals. Mutate MSB_BOZ in the J position to ONE_BOZ so the mixed-actual assertion fails by equality. Wrong-type source controls are unnumbered and expect no local diagnostic.

requirements.title: BLT result has default logical characteristics
requirements.definition: The BLT result is default logical.

pending.blt-result-default-logical: Initialize a default logical sentinel to the opposite value, assign BLT(2,1), and assert KIND(result)==KIND(.true.) plus the exact logical value from the result-value facet.

requirements.title: BLT compares bit sequences as less than
requirements.definition: BLT returns true exactly when the bit sequence represented by I is less than the bit sequence represented by J according to 16.3.2, and false otherwise.

pending.blt-true-case: Use result=.false. as a sentinel, then assert BLT(1,2) is true for nonnegative integers; mutate by swapping I and J or replacing BLT with BGT. Add the guarded BOZ discriminator BLT(1,MSB_BOZ)==.true. using the 16.9.49 p6 BOZ interpretation by 7.7 plus the 16.3.2 comparison, where MSB_BOZ is a z-bit BOZ sequence with its leftmost bit set and z=BIT_SIZE(0).
pending.blt-false-case: Use result=.true. as a sentinel, then assert BLT(2,1) and the equality discriminator BLT(2,2) are false; the equality subcase distinguishes BLT from BLE. Add the guarded BOZ discriminator BLT(MSB_BOZ,1)==.false. using the 16.9.49 p6 BOZ interpretation by 7.7 plus the 16.3.2 comparison, where MSB_BOZ is a z-bit BOZ sequence with its leftmost bit set and z=BIT_SIZE(0).
